question: GQ-007
subject: the search interface — the reason the indexes exist
the_gap: I built a 122,553-passage index, then a modern-spelling index that doubles recall, and NOTHING read either. Both were reachable only by someone who knew the vault path and wrote their own SQL. Third instance of this defect today: outbox messages, corpus counts, now the indexes themselves.

three_bugs_found_by_running_it.what: snippet() inside json_group_array threw "unable to use function snippet in the requested context"
three_bugs_found_by_running_it.cause: FTS5 auxiliary functions only work in the query that owns the MATCH
three_bugs_found_by_running_it.fix: compute the snippet in a subquery, aggregate outside

three_bugs_found_by_running_it.what: every result came from the printed index; the modern one never appeared
three_bugs_found_by_running_it.cause: concatenating printed-then-modern fills the whole page from the first index
both indexes match the SAME rows first, so dedup drops the modern duplicates before any modern-only hit is reached
three_bugs_found_by_running_it.fix: ask the modern index only for passages the printed index CANNOT find, excluded in SQL
three_bugs_found_by_running_it.why_it_matters: 1,963 passages containing "himfelf" are findable only through the modern index. Without this the recall gain exists in the table and never reaches a reader.

verified.positive: "parliament AND debate" surfaces a 1742 London Magazine debate
verified.long_s_recovery: "himself" now returns Miscellanies passages whose printed text reads "himfelf"
verified.adversarial: "zxqwvblorptik" -> no matches, AND names which indexes were searched so "not found" cannot be read as "not searched"
